requires.desc: Aggregated claims file assembled from verified era records + dataset (built at R5 start)

invariants.text: All 10 chapters plus thread-candidates.md exist per the chapter map.
All four readability tests pass on every chapter (FK <= 10, Reading Ease >= 50, Fog <= 12, SMOG <= 12), with scores recorded in frontmatter.
Every chapter's frontmatter lists the claim IDs it uses; every listed ID exists in claims.json; no chapter states a number whose claim was rejected.

Chapters preserve calibration honesty: contested numbers show their contest (competing series side by side for the capture question), CIs and grades surface where the reader needs them, and no chapter asserts what a verified claim only bounds. Jargon is explained at first use.
invariants.instructions: Read each chapter against its claims. An asserted point value for a claim that carries a wide CI, a capture-question chapter that hides one of the competing series, or unexplained jargon a general reader would not know — each violates this invariant.

invariants.text: thread-candidates.md presents each candidate thread with the schema fields and claim IDs that support it, sufficient for the human to select first-class threads at Gate B; the data layer is freezable (claims.json complete and internally consistent).
invariants.instructions: Check every candidate thread names its supporting claims and that claims.json passes its own consistency check (run python3 tools/verify_p2.py r5-claimsfile and weigh its output).

invariants.text: No claim statement quotes a value that R3 superseded. Nothing else compares a claim's prose against its own central, so an adjusted number can be corrected in the value and left stale in the text.
No chapter's prose quotes a value that R3 superseded for a claim it cites. r5-traceability proves the cited ids exist but never reads the numbers in the prose.
